The dataset included a total number of 8,236 crashes, with a limited number of variables describing the basic crash information. Among the records, there are 350 crashes with no location information provided. The City of Somerville makes certain crime data available to the public on the City’s website (City of Somerville, n.d.). The team downloaded the entire public crime data from the website, which included information describing the location, report time, and offense type for four types of crimes between 2009 and February 4, 2019: • Burglary/breaking and entering, • Motor vehicle theft, • Theft from motor vehicle, and • Robbery. The dataset included a total of 8,666 records, including 63 without location information. Like the Cambridge data, the crash and crime ratios were considered by census group. For comparison purposes, the study also collected field lighting data at selected roadways in Somerville. The lighting measurement sites were selected primarily based on several factors: • Roadway and traffic characteristics. The project team considered both major roadways and local roads. The two types of roadways represent different characteristics to be addressed during this project. Major roadways. Such roadways generally have a higher speed limit, o larger traffic volume, better traffic control, and a significant volume of inter-city or through traffic. Some major roadways may also be maintained by the state instead of the city, which may have different maintenance and operations practices. Small, local roads. The smaller, local roadways typically have fewer lanes, o lower speed limit, and less access control. Local roadways also primarily serve local traffic. 39 • Crash and crime rates. Nighttime crash and crime rates can be an indicator of nighttime activities along a roadway segment. They can also potentially reveal any effects the ALS has on users.
